areas.name: Limits on destructive and reserved acts
areas.covers: What a session may never do unattended (deploy, production data, credentials, admin) and what mc may delete or overwrite.

questions.when: The change lets a session do something it could not do before, or removes or narrows a refusal.
questions.ask: Which roles can now do it headless, and do the deploy, production-data, credential and admin refusals still hold for every one of them?

questions.when: The change deletes, overwrites or moves files, branches, worktrees or records it did not itself create.
questions.ask: What proves ownership and that nothing live, dirty or unpushed is lost, and what does it do when that proof is missing?

areas.name: The session roles and their instructions
areas.covers: The canon: roles, verbs and task pages, and the code that installs and guards them.

questions.when: The change alters what a role may or must do.
questions.ask: Do the role's page, the verb's page, the guard in the code and docs/technical say the same thing, and does a session working from the old words get a refusal that names the new way?

questions.when: The change adds a sentence to canon/.
questions.ask: Is the rule already stated in another canon file (one home per rule), and does the page stay within its length?

areas.name: The command's contract
areas.covers: Verbs, flags, exit codes, help, and the file formats mc reads and writes.

questions.when: The change adds or alters a verb, a flag or an exit code.
questions.ask: Does --help say it, does a refused call exit 2 having written nothing and name the call that works, and is the route walked by the help-routes test?

questions.when: The change alters a file format mc reads or writes.
questions.ask: What does an mc of the version before do with the new file, and what does this version do with every file of the old form on disk?

areas.name: Tests and gate
areas.covers: Test protection, and what gate, the merger and the daily run select, measure and reuse.

questions.when: The change adds, alters or retires a test.
questions.ask: Which behaviour does it protect and what fails for a user when that breaks, is its level the cheapest credible one, and was the protection commissioned?

questions.when: The change alters what gate, the merger or the daily run selects or reuses.
questions.ask: Which red can now pass unmeasured, and where is it still measured?

areas.name: Operations
areas.covers: The runner, the merger and the installed mc: long-lived processes, state on disk, loops and restarts.

questions.when: The change alters the runner, the merger or data they read.
questions.ask: A process started before the update keeps its code: what does it do with the new data until it is restarted, and what does the new code do with the state the old one left?

questions.when: The change adds a loop, a relaunch or a retry.
questions.ask: What stops it when nothing changes between attempts, and where is the stop reported?

areas.name: Documentation
areas.covers: The docs/technical pages that must describe what landed, and the changelog.

questions.when: The change alters behaviour a docs/technical page describes, or adds behaviour none describes.
questions.ask: Which pages and sections must say what landed, and is a changelog.d entry due?

areas.name: The system (mc)
areas.covers: mc itself as a source area: what is striven for, the decisions that hold for the system and where its assets are. It asks no stand of a goal.
